answer.read: Brandlhuber is a family foundry asking for +9.5% from 1 Nov 2026 (doc:20260911-70110-P01). That notice falls short of the contract's 90-day, calendar-year rule (ctr:4600070110#3.1). Its cost tracking is stale: the owner's spreadsheet was last updated two years ago (M1/M4), and its cited indices (labour +2.7%, castings PPI +6.5%) cover only part of its cost, while energy fell 6.1%. Should-cost of €132.64 (±5%, range down to €126.01) suggests it may genuinely be near or below cost. With a stabilise goal, its health matters to our C. It also asked for fast payment (M2), so early payment is something it values. Its delivery and quality record is weak (OTD 85.2%, an open 8D), but citing that adds little here. Its status is open, it has sent one reply, and it is anchored high at €138.55.
answer.message: Thank you for your offer and for the long partnership, which we value as well. We have reviewed your figures carefully. The increase as notified does not follow the price-change procedure in our framework agreement, and energy costs have moved in your favour over the past year. As you asked for faster payment, we propose short payment terms in return for holding the price, as set out in the attached sheet.
answer.reason: E0 is the only selectable option; every alternative term mix has an unknown supplier trade value. It offers the 14-day payment the supplier asked for, keeps the price at today's level, and lowers our C well below C_open. It is also an early counter in a fresh thread, so it is not a lowball that stalls the talks. The notice-period, energy-index and should-cost arguments challenge its stale cost basis without leaking anything.
